nodes.title: User's Victorianist background (humanities citation patterns) drove soft year boundaries in garbage scoring
nodes.description:
User background: Victorianist (19th century lit) — citations routinely go back 50-100+ years, classics and medieval scholarship even older. Hard year-boundary rules (e.g., 'reject anything before 1900') would silently drop legitimate citations.

This directly informed the decision to use soft suspicion modifiers for year ranges rather than hard exclusions, and to raise score caps only when multiple garbage signals fire together (not on year alone).

Sources:
- project.json context: 'User background: Victorianist (19th century lit) - citations routinely go back 50-100+ years, classics/medieval even older. System must handle humanities citation patterns, not just recent CS/AI papers'
- project.json decided: 'Garbage detection should use soft suspicion modifiers for years, not hard boundaries - avoid breaking humanities citations or future cutting-edge work (2028+ thesis prep)'
